title: Mother and Child (“Ina at Anak”)
creator: Fernando Amorsolo
description: This painting beautifully depicts the deep love and bond between a mother and her child. It shows the mother carefully holding her child to protect him, representing how a mother will sacrifice everything for her child. Amorsolo skillfully captured the strong relationship between a mother and her offspring in this work of art.
subject: Filipino; Mother; Child; Maternal Love; Nurturing
location: National Museum of Fine Arts, Manila, Philippines

title: Planting Rice
creator: Fernando Amorsolo
description: The artwork depicts a group of Filipino farmers, mostly women, planting rice seedlings in a rice field. It showcases Amorsolo's mastery of light, color, and detail. The painting captures the labor-intensive process of rice planting and serves as a tribute to the hard work and resilience of Filipino farmers.
subject: Filipino; Farmers; Rice
location: The Galeria De las Islas in Intramuros, Manila, Philippines

title: Returning Fisherman
creator: Fernando Amorsolo
description: The piece captures the tranquil essence of rural life in the Philippines, influenced by the artist's childhood in the coastal town of Daet. Unlike his usual sunlit depictions of farmers, this work portrays fishermen returning at dusk, with their boat gently moored as the sky is ablaze with orange and red hues. The serene atmosphere reflects the end of the day, where labor gives way to rest, all while being surrounded by the beauty of nature.
subject: Filipino; Fishermen; Shore; Dusk; Sailboats

title: Seascape
creator: Fernando Amorsolo
description: "Seascape" by Fernando Amorsolo is a painting that beautifully captures the essence of Filipino life and culture by depicting a fisher family at the end of a day's work. This artwork showcases Amorsolo's mastery of light and his talent for evoking the pastoral beauty of rural Philippines.
subject: Filipino; Fishermen; Family; Sailboats
location: National Museum of Fine Arts, Manila, Philippines

title: Lavanderas
creator: Fernando Amorsolo
description: The painting depicts a group of women engaged in the daily chore of doing laundry by a river, symbolizing the beauty and simplicity of rural life. It captures the essence of communal work and camaraderie, highlighting themes of renewal and community. Amorsolo's use of light and color enhances the scene, creating a harmonious landscape that reflects the tranquility of the Filipino countryside.
subject: Filipino; Woman; River; Washing clothes

title: Bombing of the Intendencia
creator: Fernando Amorsolo
description: This painting shows the destruction of the Intendencia building in Intramuros during World War II. Fernando Amorsolo depicts the burning ruins of the historic structure, capturing the chaos of war and the loss of Manila’s cultural heritage.
subject: Destruction; Intendencia; Intramuros; World War II

title: Under the Mango Tree
creator: Fernando Amorsolo
description: This painting depicts a serene rural scene in the Philippines, where figures rest or gather under a mango tree. Fernando Amorsolo highlights the warmth of natural sunlight and the simplicity of everyday countryside life. It reflects his signature style of idealized Filipino rural beauty and calmness.
subject: Filipino; Rural Life; Nature; Traditional

title: The Blind Man
creator: Fernando Amorsolo
description: The painting portrays a blind man navigating daily life, emphasizing human vulnerability and resilience. Amorsolo presents the figure with sensitivity, focusing on dignity despite physical limitation. The work reflects compassion toward ordinary people in rural Filipino settings.
subject: Filipino; Blind Individual; Rural Life; Nature

title: Harvest
creator: Fernando Amorsolo
description: This painting depicts Filipino farmers engaged in harvesting crops in a rural field. Fernando Amorsolo emphasizes light, movement, and the harmony of rural labor. It reflects a hopeful and idealized view of agricultural life in the Philippines. The scene also highlights the importance of farming as a source of livelihood and cultural identity.
subject: Filipino; Farmers; Harvest

title: Nude
creator: Fernando Amorsolo
description: This painting presents a classical nude study of a female figure, rendered in Fernando Amorsolo’s soft, realistic style. It emphasizes natural light, form, and the gentle curves of the human body rather than dramatic expression. The work reflects Amorsolo’s academic training and interest in idealized human beauty.
subject: Filipino; Nude; Woman

title: Spoliarium
creator: Juan Luna
description: This painting depicts dying gladiators stripped of weapons and garments after a gladiatorial combat in the basement of a Roman area, being dragged on the ground.
subject: Roman Gladiatorial Match; Roman
location: National Museum of Fine Arts, Manila, Philippines

title: The Death of Cleopatra
creator: Juan Luna
description: This artwork depicts Cleopatra’s moments after her death, lying on a bed adorned with a golden headboard and covered with rich bedsheets, with the sheets themselves decorated with hieroglyphs and the footboard similarly adorned in gold.
subject: Cleopatra VII; Egypt

title: The Battle of Lepanto
creator: Juan Luna
description: The painting portrays the Battle of Lepanto of October 7, 1571, featuring Don Juan of Austria in battle while at the bow of a ship.
subject: Holy League; Ottoman Empire

title: The Parisian Life
creator: Juan Luna
description: This piece portrays a woman either a courtesan that represents “fallen womanhood”, who was about to rise from a couch overshadowing three men placed at the far left corner inside a café in Paris.
subject: Courtesan Woman
location: National Museum of Fine Arts, Manila, Philippines

title: El Pacto de Sangre (The Blood Compact)
creator: Juan Luna
description: "El Pacto de Sangre" or called the "The Blood Compact"portrays the 1565 Sandugo (blood compact ritual) between Datu Sikatuna of Bohol and Miguel López de Legazpi, surrounded by other conquistadors.
subject: Datu Sikatuna; Miguel López de Legazpi

title: España y Filipinas (Spain and the Philippines)
creator: Juan Luna
description: España y Filipinas portrays two women side by side embarking up a staircase. The left figure represents Spain, the right figure represents the Philippines. This artwork represents the "benevolent image of colonialism” guiding the “humbly dressed Filipina” towards the “right way”.
subject: Spaniard; Filipino; Woman; Motherland

title: Tampuhan (Sulking)
creator: Juan Luna
description: Tampuhan portrays a man looking out to the street beside a Capiz-shell window leaning on the ventanilla while a woman is seen sitting on a chair with a downturned gaze, they are engaged in a lover’s quarrel in the sala (living room) of a “Bahay na Bato”.
subject: Emiliana Trinidad; Ariston Bautista Lin

title: Las Damas Romanas (The Roman Dames)
creator: Juan Luna
description: Las Damas Romanas depicted a domestic scene in ancient Roman life, portraying two women lying on the steps of a house. The hand of one woman was holding the reins of two dogs in order to prevent them from scaring away some doves. The background of the painting presented a shelf of artifacts. To the left of the shelf was a shrine with a pediment shaped like a triangle. In front of the pediment was a burner with a smoking incense.
subject: Roman Maidens

title: Hymen, oh Hyménée! (Boda Romana)
creator: Juan Luna
description: This artwork portrays a scene from a Roman wedding ritual, specifically the moment when the bride is entering the groom's chamber.
subject: Unnamed Wedding Guests; Bride; Groom

title: Una Mestiza / La mestiza en su tocador / Charing (A Mestiza, The Mestiza at her dressing table)
creator: Juan Luna
description: Una Mestiza portrays a young woman sitting up, her arms are lifted up as she attempts to fix her dark curly hair. Her attire is reminiscent of the clothing often worn by women of Juan Luna’s time.
subject: Unnamed Mestiza; possibly Rosario Melgar
location: Biblioteca Museu Víctor Balaguer, Barcelona, Spain

title: La Pintura
creator: Félix Hidalgo
description: A painting with an impressionist style inspired by the trend japonisme. A woman turning back to look at an unfinished canvas. This painting is considered a “Romantic Allegory.”
subject: Woman; Nellie Boustead

title: La Parisienne
creator: Félix Hidalgo
description: Features an elegant woman strolling outdoors holding a parasol. This painting is designed to look like a candid snapshot rather than a formal portrait.
subject: Parisian; Woman; Belle Epoque

title: Marina
creator: Félix Hidalgo
description: This painting depicts the rugged coastline of Brittany in northwestern France.
subject: Seascape

title: Bois de Boulogne
creator: Félix Hidalgo
description: This painting portrays a melancholic and tranquil landscape that captures the famous Parisian Park.
subject: Parisian; Woman

title: Seascape
creator: Félix Hidalgo
description: A painting that captures sailboats against the majestic cliffs of Etretat.
subject: Seascape; Etretat; Sailboats

title: Las Virgenes Cristianas Expuestas al Populacho
creator: Félix Hidalgo
description: This artwork depicts the persecution of Christians in ancient Rome but serves as a metaphor for the humiliation of Filipinos under Spanish colonial rule.
subject: Christians; Roman; Filipino
location: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, Manila, Philippines
